newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: CRICKET-INDIA PREPARE FOR TEST.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-INDIA PREPARE FOR TEST.

text.p: India's top order batsmen put in some fine tuning for next week's test against South Africa on the opening day of their three-day match against Eastern Province on Saturday.

Fielding their likely line-up for the test beginning next Thursday - with the notable bowling exceptions of Anil Kumble and Javagal Srinath - India reached 210 for two when torrential rain halted play shortly after tea.

On a batsman-friendly St Georges pitch, elegant left-hander Saurav Ganguly top-scored with a fluent 90 not out and opening batsman Vikram Rathore compiled a more dogged 71 in the opening match of India's South African tour.
The Eastern Province attack - 19-year-old fast bowler Mornantau Hayward in particular - generated pace and bounce but were unable to make much of an impression.
Woorkeri Raman was removed for 15 in the 10th over but Rathore and Ganguly embarked on a relentless second-wicket stand of 142 either side of lunch.
Ganguly survived a sharp chance to second slip when yet to score and was struck twice in three balls by Hayward, but square drove with immaculate timing and reached 50 off 125 balls.
Rathore, who hoisted the slow left-arm of Tim Shaw for two huge sixes, eventually departed for a painstaking 71 after almost four hours, having hit three sixes and seven fours during his innings.
